newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends down after moving tightly.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends down after moving tightly.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil prices ended marginally lower after consolidating for the greater part of the day in the absence of fresh developments, traders said.
News of the November 1-25 palm oil export data by cargo surveyor SGS (M) Sdn Bhd had no impact as the market felt that the export data was within market expectations.
Malaysia's palm oil exports for November 1-25 were at 555,070 tonnes was against 615,327 tonnes for October 1-25.

"Prices were drifting in a tight range. SGS"s Nov 1-25 palm oil exports had no impact on the market," a trader said, adding that the market expects to consolidate slightly above the 1,200 levels (February futures).
At the close, the contract was three ringgit down at 1,209 ringgit ($478.70) a tonne after moving within a 11-ringgit range. The immediate support is at 1,200 ringgit.
Falls in other futures contract were also small.
"It has been a slow moving day with big participation staying away from the market. People are waiting for leads," another trader said.
Prices are expected to hold above the 1,200 ringgit on expectation of fresh export business this week. "There was talk of an Egyptian tender this week," the dealer said.
Turnover on the futures market fell further to 644 lots from 970 lots on Friday.
Among physical, Nov (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,215 ringgit with bids at 1,207.50 after trading at 1,210, and Nov (central) at 1,205 against 1,195.
Dec (south) saw offers at 1,222.50 ringgit and bids at 1,215 and earlier trades were 1,225 to 1,217.50, and Dec (central) was at 1,212.50 against 1,200.
